summary: The read-only pivot removes the round-1 problems: no shared human logins, no MFA seeds, no tier circumvention, no admin-credential vault. Remaining issues are ordinary data-protection hygiene, now concentrated in the concierge scan and emailed CSV exports (whole user lists sent before any DPA), plus contract wording so 'checks run' never reads as a guarantee.

objections.objection: The riskiest-assumption test has 20 prospects send 90 days of IdP deactivations plus full user exports from 5-10 apps, diffed by hand in a spreadsheet, before the company has a DPA, sub-processor list, retention rule or SOC 2. That is personal data on employees and leavers, processed by a vendor that may not yet exist as a company. Under GDPR Art. 28 the controller may use only processors that give sufficient guarantees, under a contract. Many IT managers' own policies will stop them sharing this, and those who do share it create exposure for both sides.

Emailed and uploaded app exports usually contain every column the app exports (names, titles, last login, sometimes billing or guest/external-collaborator data). Matching only needs identifier, status and role. Without column stripping on ingest, a fixed retention period and a non-email upload path, this breaks Art. 5(1)(c) minimisation and storage limitation. Email inboxes are also a leaky place to receive directory dumps.

A read-only list-users token is still a full directory of the customer's staff, guests and contractors in each app. Many of them are an admin-scoped token with a read label, and the concept says it will 'confine' some admin tokens rather than refuse them outright. A hosted multi-tenant store of these tokens is still a breach target, though far less dangerous than write credentials. The concept needs a published per-app scope list and a rule that admin-only tokens are refused, not just isolated.

The liability limits ('checks run', no guarantee of completeness) are listed only as a risk and are not yet in the MVP or the auditor-export wording. The free scan's 'leftover-accounts report' will also be read as a finding of fact. If a mismatch makes a customer chase or wrongly accuse an app owner, or misses a live account, customers will cite the report. The terms need disclaimers, and the report has to show which apps were and weren't covered.

strongest_point: Read-only, customer-authorised verification that never writes, stores no human logins or MFA seeds and needs no browser automation: low dual-use potential and little vendor-terms exposure.
what_would_change_my_mind: A one-page DPA, NDA and 30-day deletion commitment signed before any concierge scan, with exports cut to identifier, status and role columns.
A published per-app table for the 12 connectors showing a genuinely read-only scope on the tiers buyers hold, with admin-only apps routed to exports.
Customer terms and report templates reviewed by counsel, stating coverage per app and disclaiming completeness.

resolved_prior.objection: Browser-agent fallback replays shared human admin logins and MFA seeds that vendor terms (Figma, GitHub) forbid.
resolved_prior.note: Browser agents, stored admin passwords and TOTP seeds are out of scope. Access is through API tokens the customer issues, or exports.

resolved_prior.objection: Positioning as a way around SCIM paywalls invites circumvention claims (Atlassian s.2.2(g)).
resolved_prior.note: The product no longer provisions, and the 'SCIM tax' pitch is gone. Reading user lists through permitted APIs or exports gets around no tier limit.

resolved_prior.objection: A multi-tenant vault of admin credentials is a supply-chain target, and SOC 2 at launch is implausible.
resolved_prior.note: Only least-privileged read tokens are held, which greatly reduces the blast radius. Some residual directory-exposure risk remains (see objection 3), and SOC 2 is still listed among the hardest parts.

resolved_prior.objection: Selling nightly verification as 'audit evidence' creates liability if a connector silently misses a deprovision.
resolved_prior.note: The log now records 'checks run' without claiming completeness. The contract terms still need to be written (see objection 4).

resolved_prior.objection: GDPR processor duties, and admin-console screenshots retained as excessive evidence.
resolved_prior.note: With no browser agents there are no screenshots, and DPAs, a sub-processor list and short retention are now in the risks. CSV exports bring a smaller minimisation issue back (objection 2).
